description: From the physics of silicon to working amplifier and logic circuits, with every circuit built, measured and simulated rather than only drawn. Taught to the depth of a first-year engineering circuits course, with every circuit simulated and measured.
modelledOn: Agarwal and Lang, Foundations of Analog and Digital Electronic Circuits
Boylestad and Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory
outcomes: Analyse DC and AC circuits with Kirchhoff's laws, node and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton equivalents.
Explain how carriers move in doped silicon and derive the diode and transistor V-I behaviour from it.
Design rectifiers, regulators, clippers and clampers and predict their waveforms.
Bias a BJT amplifier for stable operation and compute its gain, input and output resistance.
Analyse RLC circuits in the time and frequency domains and read resonance and bandwidth from a plot.
Classify signals and relate the continuous and discrete views of them to later signal processing courses.

units.title: Circuit fundamentals and lab practice
topics: Charge, current, voltage, power and energy; passive sign convention
Resistors, Ohm's law, series and parallel combinations, voltage and current dividers
Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws; node-voltage and mesh-current analysis
Superposition, Thevenin and Norton equivalents, maximum power transfer
Using a breadboard, multimeter, oscilloscope and bench supply; reading a datasheet
Dependent sources and the ideal operational amplifier as a circuit element

units.title: Semiconductor physics
topics: Energy bands in conductors, insulators and semiconductors; band gap of silicon and germanium
Intrinsic carriers, electrons and holes; temperature dependence
Doping: donors and acceptors, n-type and p-type material, majority and minority carriers
Drift and diffusion currents; mobility and conductivity
The p-n junction at equilibrium: depletion region, built-in potential

units.title: Diodes and diode circuits
topics: Forward and reverse bias; the diode equation and the V-I curve; ideal, constant-drop and piecewise models
Zener breakdown and avalanche; Zener regulators and line/load regulation
Half-wave, full-wave centre-tap and bridge rectifiers; ripple and capacitor filters
Regulated DC supplies: transformer, rectifier, filter, regulator (78xx and LM317)
Clippers, clampers and voltage multipliers; LED and photodiode circuits
Reading a diode datasheet: PIV, forward drop, maximum current, recovery time

units.title: Bipolar junction transistors
topics: NPN and PNP structure and operation; active, saturation and cut-off regions; alpha and beta
Common-emitter, common-base and common-collector configurations and their characteristics
DC load line and Q-point; fixed, emitter and voltage-divider biasing; bias stability and thermal runaway
Small-signal model (hybrid-pi) and the gain, input and output resistance of a CE amplifier
The transistor as a switch: driving an LED, a relay and a small DC motor
Introduction to MOSFETs: enhancement-mode NMOS and PMOS, threshold voltage, regions of operation

units.title: Operational amplifiers
topics: Ideal op-amp rules; inverting, non-inverting, summing and difference amplifiers
Integrators, differentiators and active filters
Comparators, Schmitt triggers and simple oscillators
Real op-amp limits: offset, slew rate, gain-bandwidth product

units.title: Digital circuits and logic families
topics: Voltage levels, noise margins and the transfer characteristic of an inverter
Diode logic AND and OR gates and why they cannot be cascaded
RTL, DTL and TTL gate construction; totem-pole output; fan-out and propagation delay
CMOS inverter, NAND and NOR; static and dynamic power
Interfacing logic families and level shifting; open-collector and tri-state outputs

units.title: Capacitors, inductors and RLC circuits
topics: Capacitor and inductor V-I relations; energy storage; RC and RL transients and time constants
Sinusoidal steady state: phasors, impedance and admittance
Series and parallel RLC circuits: resonance frequency, quality factor, bandwidth
Frequency response and Bode plots; low-pass, high-pass and band-pass filters
Second-order transients: underdamped, critically damped and overdamped responses

units.title: Signals
topics: Continuous-time and discrete-time signals; sampling as the bridge between them
Even and odd decomposition; periodic and aperiodic signals
Energy and power signals; RMS value of common waveforms
Standard signals: impulse, step, ramp, exponential and sinusoid
Reading a signal on an oscilloscope: amplitude, period, frequency, phase, DC offset

schedule.title: Charge, current, voltage and resistor networks
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute current, voltage and power for ten resistor networks, including a series-parallel network and a divider, and check the power balance (supplied equals absorbed) in each.

tasks.title: Build a 9 V battery with three series resistors, predict each voltage drop with the divider rule, then measure all three with the virtual multimeter
Build a series-parallel network of five resistors, predict total current and power in each part by hand, then confirm that supplied power equals the sum absorbed
Debug a given eight-resistor ladder whose measured node voltages disagree with the schematic, locate the wrong resistor value by node-voltage analysis and correct it

schedule.title: Network theorems, instruments and the ideal op-amp
schedule.exercise: Reduce a bridge circuit to a Thevenin equivalent on paper, then write a half-page lab note listing which instrument settings you would use to verify it on a bench.

tasks.title: Measure a 5 V rail and a 1 kHz square wave with the virtual multimeter and oscilloscope, and record the readings in a table with units
Find the Thevenin equivalent of a two-source network by simulation, then load it with ten resistor values and plot power to confirm maximum power transfer
Design an ideal op-amp stage that turns a 0 to 1 V sensor signal into 0 to 5 V, then verify gain and output limits in the simulator

schedule.title: Semiconductor physics and the p-n junction
schedule.exercise: Short written exercise: compute intrinsic carrier concentration of silicon at 300 K and 350 K, explain the change, and sketch the band diagrams of n-type and p-type silicon.

tasks.title: Plot the intrinsic carrier concentration of silicon against temperature from 250 K to 400 K and read off the values at 300 K and 350 K
Compute electron and hole concentrations for silicon doped with 1e16 per cm3 donors at 300 K, then repeat for acceptors and compare the majority carriers
Calculate the built-in potential and depletion width of a p-n junction for three doping pairs, plot them, and explain which doping gives the narrowest depletion region

schedule.title: Diode characteristics and rectifiers
schedule.exercise: Problem set: solve three diode circuits with the ideal, constant-drop and piecewise models, compare answers, and design a Zener regulator for a 5.1 V load drawing 10 to 40 mA.

tasks.title: Trace the V-I curve of a silicon diode from -2 V to 1 V and mark the knee voltage and the reverse-bias region
Build a bridge rectifier with a smoothing capacitor driven by a 12 V AC source and measure ripple voltage for three capacitor values
Design a Zener regulator for a 9 V input and 5.1 V load from 10 to 40 mA, then measure line and load regulation across the whole range

schedule.title: Power supplies, clippers and diode datasheets
schedule.exercise: Reading exercise: from two diode datasheets pick the better part for a 230 V mains bridge rectifier, justifying each choice with PIV, forward current and recovery time.

tasks.title: Build a diode clipper that limits a 5 V peak sine to 2.7 V and view input and output together on the oscilloscope
Assemble transformer, bridge, filter capacitor and an LM7805 regulator, then measure output voltage while load current steps from 0 to 500 mA
Choose the diode for a 230 V rectifier from three datasheet extracts, then simulate the circuit to verify peak inverse voltage and current stay inside the limits

schedule.title: Bipolar transistors: operation and configurations
schedule.exercise: Problem set: given measured base, collector and emitter currents for six transistors, compute alpha and beta and state the operating region of each.

tasks.title: Plot collector current against collector-emitter voltage for four base currents and label the cut-off, active and saturation regions
Measure the input resistance and voltage gain of a common-emitter stage, then compare them with a common-collector stage built on the same transistor
Given a transistor stage that clips its output, identify which configuration and region of operation is wrong from the waveforms, and redesign it to be undistorted

schedule.title: Biasing and the small-signal amplifier
schedule.exercise: Design exercise: choose resistors for a voltage-divider biased common-emitter stage at 2 mA collector current with 12 V supply, then predict the small-signal gain.

tasks.title: Bias an NPN transistor with a fixed-bias resistor, read the Q-point, and mark it on the DC load line
Design a voltage-divider bias network for a 2 mA collector current and show that the Q-point barely moves when beta changes from 100 to 300
Build a common-emitter amplifier with voltage gain near -50, measure gain, input and output resistance, and explain any difference from the hybrid-pi prediction

schedule.title: Transistor switches and MOSFETs
schedule.exercise: Calculate the base resistor, flyback diode and supply for switching a 12 V relay with a 5 V microcontroller pin, and state the worst-case current that the pin must supply.

tasks.title: Wire an NPN transistor and base resistor to an Arduino pin to switch an LED, and compute the base resistor value first
Drive a 12 V relay and a small DC motor from Arduino pins using a transistor and flyback diode, and verify that the pin current stays below 20 mA
Plot the drain current against gate voltage for an NMOS device, extract the threshold voltage, and build a MOSFET switch that turns on fully at 5 V

schedule.title: Operational amplifier circuits and limits
schedule.exercise: Problem set: design amplifiers with gains of -10 and +11 and a three-input summer, state the output at given inputs and the saturation point for a 12 V supply.

tasks.title: Build an inverting amplifier of gain -10, apply a 0.2 V sine, and check that the output amplitude and phase match the prediction
Build a first-order active low-pass filter with a 1 kHz cut-off and plot its gain at ten frequencies to confirm the roll-off
Drive a non-inverting amplifier of gain 100 over increasing frequency and amplitude, find the gain-bandwidth limit and slew-rate limit, and explain each failure

schedule.title: Digital circuits and logic families
schedule.exercise: Short report comparing TTL and CMOS on noise margin, power and speed, with a table of the datasheet values you used and a worked noise-margin calculation.

tasks.title: Plot the transfer characteristic of a CMOS inverter and mark VIL, VIH, VOL and VOH to calculate both noise margins
Build CMOS NAND and NOR gates from transistors and verify all four input combinations in the truth table, then estimate dynamic power at 1 MHz
Interface a 3.3 V sensor output to a 5 V logic input using open-collector gates and a pull-up, then test it at every logic level and edge

schedule.title: Capacitors, inductors and RLC resonance
schedule.exercise: Calculations on paper: time constant of an RC and an RL circuit, phasor impedance of a series RLC at three frequencies, and resonance frequency, Q and bandwidth.

tasks.title: Charge a capacitor through a 10 kOhm resistor from a 5 V step, read the time constant from the scope trace and compare it with RC
Compute and plot the impedance magnitude and phase of a series RL circuit from 10 Hz to 100 kHz using complex numbers
Build a series RLC circuit that resonates at 10 kHz, measure its resonance, Q and bandwidth, and retune it to a 2 kHz bandwidth

schedule.title: Frequency response and second-order transients
schedule.exercise: Sketch asymptotic Bode plots for a first-order low-pass and a second-order system, and write which damping ratio gives each of the three transient types.

tasks.title: Sweep a first-order RC low-pass filter and read the cut-off frequency at -3 dB from the Bode plot
Plot Bode magnitude and phase for cascaded high-pass and low-pass sections, and report the resulting band-pass gain, centre frequency and bandwidth
Tune the resistor of a series RLC circuit to produce underdamped, critically damped and overdamped step responses, and measure the overshoot of each

schedule.title: Signals and measurements on the oscilloscope
schedule.exercise: Exercise: for five given waveforms (sine, square, triangle, sawtooth, pulse train) compute the RMS value, period, frequency and DC offset by hand, then check them in the simulator.

tasks.title: Read amplitude, period, frequency and DC offset from a given scope trace of an offset sine wave, and record all four values
Compute the RMS value of square, triangle and sine waves numerically and check each against its closed-form formula to within 1 percent
Sample a 50 Hz sine at five different rates, plot the sampled signals, and find the lowest rate at which the original frequency can still be recovered
